validity.researcher_notes: IDENTITY CHECK (per dispatch instructions): 'Centra' most commonly refers to Centra Gas Manitoba (a Manitoba Hydro local-distribution utility), but that is NOT what this row describes. P7125's sheet values (Owner1='Energy Fundamentals Group LP', StartLocation='Spruce Siding', StartState/Province='Manitoba', EndLocation='Fort Frances', EndState/Province='Ontario', 270 km, 12-inch) match a distinct entity: the 'Centra Gas Transmission System' / 'Centra Pipelines', a 270 km, NPS 12.75-inch interstate/international natural gas TRANSMISSION pipeline built in 1970, owned by Energy Fundamentals Group LP (EFGLP) and operated through two subsidiaries — Centra Transmission Holdings Inc. (CTHI, the Canadian portion, regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator/CER) and Centra Pipelines Minnesota Inc. (CPMI, the Minnesota portion, regulated by FERC). This is why the row correctly sits in the US gas tracker despite Canadian termini: CPMI is an active FERC-jurisdictional interstate pipeline (confirmed by a Federal Register combined notice of filings dated 2026-04-23 naming 'Centra Pipelines Minnesota Inc.', Docket RP26-765-000, filed 4/17/26, and by an earlier 1996 Federal Register notice, Docket RP97-33-000, naming 'Centra Pipelines Minnesota Inc. (Centra Minnesota)' — so CPMI has been a FERC-regulated entity since at least 1996) and by PHMSA, which lists 'CENTRA PIPELINE MINNESOTA INC.' as Operator ID 31024, 'Currently Active Operator ID'. The Canadian side (CTHI) is independently confirmed to exist and operate by a 2018 Canada Energy Regulator inspection-officer order (TC-001-2018) addressing construction of CTHI's 'Tribes Rock Replacement Project' near Emo, Ontario. EXISTENCE is therefore corroborated by 4 mutually-independent government records (US Federal Register x2, US PHMSA, Canadian CER) spanning 1996-2026, none of them GEM or centrapipelines.com/efgroupllc.com. CLASSIFICATION (transmission) is correct per both the operator's and EFG's own description ('natural gas transmission pipeline system'). DUPLICATE check against the 42-row roster: no other row describes this system (the nearest analog, P2625 Tioga to Emerson, is a different, separate Manitoba-North Dakota shelved project) — not a duplicate. Route geojson (1 feature, 89 points) runs from (-96.15,49.66) near Spruce Siding, MB to (-93.42,48.61) near Fort Frances, ON, consistent with the sourced corridor. Caveat: see the separate attribution concern on the true EndLocation.

validity.recommendation: verify true system terminus — the pipeline reportedly loops back into Minnesota, terminating at International Falls, MN, USA, not at Fort Frances, ON, Canada
validity.researcher_notes: Both the operator's own about-us page (via Wayback capture 2025-05-03) and the CER-hosted company fact sheet describe the pipeline's route as: 'takes gas from the TC Energy pipeline at Spruce Siding, Manitoba south of Lake of the Woods through Minnesota into Ontario and back into Minnesota at International Falls' / '...travels south of Lake of the Woods, through northeastern Minnesota, into Ontario and back into Minnesota, terminating at International Falls.' Both sources are explicit that the single 270 km asset crosses the US-Canada border three times (Manitoba->Minnesota->Ontario->Minnesota) and that its far terminus is International Falls, MN, USA — not Fort Frances, ON, which is only the point where the line re-enters Ontario partway along the route (also named as a served Ontario community in the home page and fact sheet, alongside Rainy River, Stratton, Barwick, Emo, Devlin). The digitized route (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P7125.geojson, 1 feature, 89 points) also stops at Fort Frances (-93.42234,48.61399) and does not extend to International Falls — so the geometry is a partial trace of the same asset, consistent with the sheet's shorter, plausibly-incomplete endpoint. This is single-origin (both text sources trace to the same company/EFG family; a second, independent source stating 'International Falls' specifically as the far terminus was searched for — FERC eLibrary docket text, NEB/CER historical orders, press — but not found before the session's web-search budget was exhausted), so I am flagging rather than correcting outright: recommend verifying against CPMI's FERC tariff (which would state the certificated end point) or a CER facilities application before changing EndLocation/EndState/EndCountryOrArea. If confirmed, the route geojson is also a candidate for extension under §8 (not fabricated here).
